input.plan:
# Semantic workflow color palette

The board UX is fine. The colors are not carrying meaning.

Warm Horizon collapsed every semantic alias onto logo navy and orange. That is why **Looking to apply** and **Waiting referral** are the same chip, **Seen before** is a quieter navy, and **Mark rejected** / **Not for me** sit next to brand orange on the hue wheel.

```37:43:relocation_jobs/static/design-tokens.css
  --accent-blue: var(--color-ink-2);
  --accent-purple: var(--color-ink);
  --accent-green: oklch(42% 0.09 145);
  ...
  --accent-blue-soft: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ink-2) 12%, var(--color-paper));
  --accent-purple-soft: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-rule) 12%, var(--color-paper));
```

```107:108:relocation_jobs/static/design-tokens.css
  --referral: var(--color-ink-2);
  --referral-soft: var(--accent-blue-soft);
```

`--danger` is `oklch(... 25)` (orange-red) and `--warn` is `oklch(... 55)` (orange-yellow). Both sit next to logo orange (`#ff6b35`). Success green is too low-chroma to read as “applied.”

Hallmark’s **one accent** rule stays for brand chrome. A job workbench also needs a **status layer**: small tinted chips mapped to meaning, not competing brand colors. This is the design-system three-layer model (primitive → semantic → component) and matches how Linear/GitHub keep status readable without a carnival.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph brand [Brand primitives - keep]
    paper[paper ivory]
    ink[logo navy]
    accent[logo orange]
  end
  subgraph status [Status primitives - new]
    sky[sky intent]
    green[green success]
    violet[violet pending]
    crimson[crimson danger]
    ochre[ochre dismiss]
    slate[slate memory]
  end
  subgraph semantic [Semantic aliases]
    intent[intent]
    success[success]
    pending[pending]
    danger[danger]
    dismiss[dismiss]
    memory[memory]
  end
  subgraph components [Board components]
    looking[Looking to apply]
    applied[Mark applied]
    referral[Waiting referral]
    rejected[Mark rejected]
    hide[Not for me]
    seen[Seen before]
  end
  sky --> intent --> looking
  green --> success --> applied
  violet --> pending --> referral
  crimson --> danger --> rejected
  ochre --> dismiss --> hide
  slate --> memory --> seen
```

## Direction (not a rebrand)

- Keep Warm Horizon for paper, ink, primary CTAs, marketing, focus rings.
- Add a chip-scale status set. Combined status fills stay well under Hallmark’s ~5% accent budget.
- Do not persist a new `design-system/MASTER.md`. Amend the locked system in [`design.md`](design.md) and the two token files.
- Labels already satisfy “don’t convey by color alone.” No icon pass in this change unless a button still fails the squint test after hues land.

## Status primitives (OKLCH, hue-spaced)

Hues sit ~50–70° apart so adjacent chips read as different, not “same navy, different words.” Chroma stays moderate so they look professional on ivory paper.

- **Intent / sky** `oklch(48% 0.12 240)` — Looking to apply, looking badge, looking card tint (replaces leftover `#248cfb`)
- **Success / green** `oklch(44% 0.13 150)` — Mark applied, applied badge, Restore
- **Pending / violet** `oklch(46% 0.11 295)` — Waiting referral, awaiting-response, referral badge
- **Danger / crimson** `oklch(48% 0.16 20)` — Mark rejected, rejected badge, show-rejected (true red, not orange-red)
- **Dismiss / ochre** `oklch(55% 0.13 80)` — Not for me, warn, pin, fetch-problem (ochre, not brand orange)
- **Memory / slate** `oklch(46% 0.03 250)` — Seen before, seen badge (lowest visual weight)
- **Visa / teal** `oklch(45% 0.08 195)` — Visa badge only, so it no longer shares green with Applied

Semantic aliases: `--intent`, `--success`, `--pending`, `--danger`, `--dismiss`, `--memory`, plus matching `-soft` mixes (~14% on paper). Existing `--referral`, `--warn`, `--accent-blue`, `--accent-purple` become aliases to this layer so current CSS class names keep working.

## Button states (same shape, clearer on/off)

Keep the current tinted-pill style in [`relocation_jobs/static/styles.css`](relocation_jobs/static/styles.css). Widen idle vs active:

- **Idle:** ~8% tint, 1px hue border, hue text
- **Hover:** ~14% tint
- **Active/on:** ~20% tint, stronger border

That makes “Interested” vs “Looking to apply” obvious without changing layout. Text contrast target: **4.5:1** on the tinted fill (WCAG; UX skill).

## Files

- [`design.md`](design.md) — document the status layer; relax “no purple/cyan” to **no competing brand accents**. Status chips at control scale are allowed and required for meaning.
- [`relocation_jobs/static/design-tokens.css`](relocation_jobs/static/design-tokens.css) and [`homepage/app/design-tokens.css`](homepage/app/design-tokens.css) — lockstep primitives + semantic aliases (homepage already uses `--success` / `--danger` for forms).
- [`relocation_jobs/static/styles.css`](relocation_jobs/static/styles.css) — point action buttons, badges, company toggles, and card tints at semantic tokens; remove hardcoded `#248cfb`, `oklch(40% 0.08 180)`, and `rgba(122, 168, 255, …)`.

No JS/HTML changes unless a leftover hex is inlined (none in the action markup today).

## Verify in the browser

On a real job card: idle row (Mark applied / Not for me / More) and expanded row (Looking to apply / Seen before / Waiting referral / Mark rejected). Then flip each to active. Also check company toggles, visa vs applied badges, rejected/not-for-me sections, and a 375px card so the denser row still reads as six different actions.

Add OKLCH status primitives + semantic aliases in both design-tokens.css files (lockstep)
Retarget board buttons, badges, toggles, and card tints; remove hardcoded leftover hues; strengthen idle vs active
Verify idle/active job actions, badges, and mobile row in the panel
